findings.title: Request identity lost after demand extraction
findings.description: The _internal_request_id is extracted from the taken demand but only used in the generation-mismatch coalescing case. For requests that pass the generation check and proceed through render_one(), decoder dispatch, and presentation, the ID is discarded and never propagated.
findings.evidence: Line 868: let (dynamic_demand, _internal_request_id) = match dynamic_demand_with_id { ... }; Line 875-881: ID only used inside generation-mismatch branch; Line 883+: ID never referenced in successful render path through render_one(), materialize_request(), or any async operation.
findings.consequence: Accepted requests remain in Active state indefinitely because their lifecycle identity never reaches decoder, compositor, or presentation boundaries where terminal transitions should occur. Session shutdown will abandon them, but legitimate completion paths cannot mark them Presented or handle failures.
findings.correction: 1. Remove underscore prefix from _internal_request_id to signal it must be used. 2. Thread Option<FrameRequestId> through: materialize_request() (or store alongside base_request), render_one() signature, decoder dispatch async boundary, ready-frame queue structure, produced-frame handoff. 3. Store the ID in a structure that survives until the frame is presented or fails. 4. Consider storing active request IDs in a session-level map keyed by external request_id or generation to enable lifecycle queries.
